messages:
devon: Heads-up — we started seeing a perf regression in multi-GPU runs after the kernel-selection/quant changes. Repro is stable with CI traces: graph replay triggers a host-sync that serializes allreduce, killing comm/compute overlap. nvtx shows big gaps. cc: @jess @kai

jess: Ugh. Any chance the capture stream vs comm stream got swapped during replay? Last time we saw host-sync it was because graph captured work on stream 1 but NCCL ops were issued on stream 0, and replay forced a sync. :thinking_face:

kai: Can you paste the nvtx snippet and the minimal trace? I want to see which stream the kv-cache warmup runs on vs the tensor-parallel allreduce.

devon: Pasting the condensed trace + a tiny log excerpt; repro is short (single forward / KV warmup / cross-rep allreduce).

```
# nvtx condensed (timestamps ms since start)
[  12.3 ] kernel: fwd_layer_1 (stream=1)
[  12.7 ] nvtx: kv_prefetch (stream=1)
[  13.1 ] kernel: fwd_layer_2 (stream=1)
[  13.4 ] ncclAllReduce start (stream=0)
[  13.4 ] cuda_graph: begin_replay (stream=1)
[  13.5 ] cuda_graph: host_sync - forced
[  13.8 ] ncclAllReduce end (stream=0)
# log
2025-11-12T15:04:10Z INFO kernel_selector: picked quantized-kernel-v3 for seq=256
2025-11-12T15:04:10Z DEBUG graph: replay -> host_sync(reason=stream-mismatch)
2025-11-12T15:04:10Z WARN allreduce: queued on stream 0, replay on stream 1 -> blocking
```

devon: Repro command: `python -m perf.repro --model=gpt2-small --bs=8 --use_cuda_graphs --kv_warmup=on --profile=nvtx`

jess: If the capture was created while some ops were placed on the default (0) stream, replay will implicitly synchronize. Two quick experiments: (1) force all NCCL launches onto the same stream used in capture (e.g., set comm_stream = compute_stream), (2) disable cuda graphs for the kv-warmup path and only capture the pure forward. Which one is cheaper to try?

kai: Also check the capture mode: if we used cudaStreamCaptureModeGlobal it can lead to unexpected host-syncs during replay when the runtime inserts event dependencies. Try ThreadLocal or ensure the capture scopes include explicit NCCL launches.

devon: Tried (1) locally — binding comm to compute stream drops the host_sync and overlap is restored (tokens/sec +18%). Looks like graph replay currently rewrites scheduling in a way that stops NCCL from running concurrently.

jess: Okay, next steps: (A) add a unit repro in eng-runtime perf suite that asserts no host_sync in nvtx for the simple forward+allreduce case; (B) short-term fallback: detect stream mismatch at compile-time and avoid capturing that mixed path; (C) longer term: kernel selector should prefer stream-consistent enqueuing for kv prefetch. I can take (A)+(B).

kai: I'll follow up with a small patch that ensures NCCL launches are pinned to the capture stream when graphs are enabled (guarded behind a flag). We should also add an nvtx marker around nccl ops so traces clearly show which stream they use.

infra-bot: perf-runner: scheduled job perf/eng-runtime/graph-replay-hostsync-1755009000 (queue=short), will post artifacts to CI when done. :rocket:

devon: Thanks — I'll open a regression ticket and attach the nvtx trace + repro script. If jess/kai could coordinate the patch + test, we can roll a canary patch to Dedicated later today. :thumbsup:

jess: ACK. I'll start the test and write the flaky guard to disable capture for kv-warmup when streams are inconsistent.

kai: Will draft the NCCL pinning patch and add the NVTX markers. Ping me if infra-bot posts the CI flamegraph.

devon: Filed: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-1428 — summary: "graph replay host-sync blocks allreduce (stream mismatch)". Assigning to @jess and @kai.

jess: :eyes: will update by EOD.
